count_reason: Fifteen distinct failure ideas matter for a suction climber on this facade: adhesion, wind, energy, cleaning, joints, obstacles, a moving cradle and glass edges. Three or four worlds each spread from mild to harsh gives 49.

scenarios.name: suction_slightly_reduced
scenarios.reason: Slightly weaker suction reduces the grip that holds the robot on the glass and may start slow slipping.

scenarios.name: suction_moderately_reduced
scenarios.reason: Moderately weak suction may leave too little friction to carry the robot's weight while climbing.

scenarios.name: suction_severely_reduced
scenarios.reason: Very weak suction may let the robot slide down or detach from the glass.

scenarios.name: seal_leak_small_increase
scenarios.reason: A slightly larger leak takes away some of the vacuum margin the robot relies on.

scenarios.name: seal_leak_worn_skirt
scenarios.reason: A worn skirt leaks enough air that the pump may not hold the pressure needed to grip.

scenarios.name: seal_leak_torn_skirt
scenarios.reason: A torn skirt may lose so much vacuum that the robot can no longer stay attached.

scenarios.name: glass_slightly_wetter
scenarios.reason: A little more water lowers friction between the drive and the glass and may add some slip.

scenarios.name: local_wet_runoff_patch
scenarios.reason: A sudden wet patch can drop traction partway up a lane and cause an abrupt slide.

scenarios.name: glass_fully_soaked
scenarios.reason: Fully soaked glass may leave too little traction for the robot to climb or hold position.

scenarios.name: steady_wind_small_rise
scenarios.reason: A slightly stronger steady wind adds a small constant load against the grip.

scenarios.name: gusts_moderately_stronger
scenarios.reason: Stronger gusts from a different angle may push the robot sideways out of its lane.

scenarios.name: fresh_wind_with_strong_gusts
scenarios.reason: Fresh wind with repeated strong gusts may overcome friction and cause drift or sliding.

scenarios.name: gale_with_violent_gusts
scenarios.reason: Gale force wind with violent gusts may pull the robot off the glass completely.

scenarios.name: battery_partly_used
scenarios.reason: Starting with a somewhat used battery reduces the reserve for the full job.

scenarios.name: battery_about_one_third
scenarios.reason: With a third of the charge the robot may run out of energy before finishing all lanes.

scenarios.name: battery_nearly_empty
scenarios.reason: A nearly empty battery may stop the pump and drive early and leave the robot stranded on the glass.

scenarios.name: work_area_slightly_larger
scenarios.reason: A slightly larger area adds lanes and travel, which uses up more time and energy.

scenarios.name: work_area_much_larger
scenarios.reason: A much larger area means longer climbs and more lanes, which may expose drift and energy limits.

scenarios.name: work_area_maximum_size
scenarios.reason: The largest area may exceed what one charge can cover and let lane errors build up.

scenarios.name: overall_dirt_small_rise
scenarios.reason: Slightly heavier dirt may leave faint residue after the normal number of passes.

scenarios.name: local_grime_patch
scenarios.reason: A local band of thicker grime may survive a pass that is enough for the surrounding glass.

scenarios.name: heavy_dirt_with_baked_grime
scenarios.reason: Heavy dirt everywhere plus baked grime may be far more than the pad can remove in one job.

scenarios.name: clean_speed_slightly_faster
scenarios.reason: A slightly faster pass removes less dirt and demands more grip from the drive.

scenarios.name: clean_speed_much_faster
scenarios.reason: A notably faster pass may start leaving dirt and reduce the margin for traction.

scenarios.name: clean_speed_at_cap
scenarios.reason: Running at the speed cap sits close to where the robot may become unstable and clean poorly.

scenarios.name: joints_slightly_deeper_wider
scenarios.reason: Slightly larger joints let a little air under the skirt as the robot crosses them.

scenarios.name: joints_moderately_deep_shifted
scenarios.reason: Deeper, wider joints in a shifted position may cause a brief vacuum dip at each crossing.

scenarios.name: joints_deepest_and_widest
scenarios.reason: The deepest and widest joints, placed more often, may break the seal and drop the robot.

scenarios.name: tiny_frame_step
scenarios.reason: A tiny frame step may lift the skirt slightly as the robot passes over it.

scenarios.name: larger_frame_step
scenarios.reason: A larger step may tilt the body and open a leak path under the skirt.

scenarios.name: metal_window_sill
scenarios.reason: A metal sill may be too tall to cross and could stall the robot or break its seal.

scenarios.name: concrete_ledge_across_area
scenarios.reason: A concrete ledge across every lane may block the robot and trap it or cause it to detach.

scenarios.name: small_tenant_nameplate
scenarios.reason: The robot knows nothing about objects, so even a small plate may catch its body in one lane.

scenarios.name: vertical_shading_fin
scenarios.reason: A vertical fin may wedge the robot against its side or force it out of its lane.

scenarios.name: window_air_conditioner
scenarios.reason: A bulky air conditioner in a lane may stop the robot dead and push it off line.

scenarios.name: balcony_slab_across_area
scenarios.reason: A balcony slab across all lanes blocks every climb and may leave glass uncleaned or jam the robot.

scenarios.name: small_exhaust_louvre
scenarios.reason: A small open louvre may let some air in under the skirt as the robot passes.

scenarios.name: medium_air_intake_grille
scenarios.reason: A larger grille may vent enough of the suction chamber to cause a sharp grip loss.

scenarios.name: wide_open_plant_room_louvre
scenarios.reason: A wide, mostly open louvre may collapse the vacuum across several lanes and release the robot.

scenarios.name: parked_cradle_near_edge
scenarios.reason: A stationary cradle near the area edge may touch the robot in the outer lane.

scenarios.name: slow_moving_cradle
scenarios.reason: A cradle moving slowly through the area may strike the robot, which cannot sense it.

scenarios.name: fast_wide_cradle_sweep
scenarios.reason: A wide cradle sweeping quickly over the whole area may knock the robot off the glass.

scenarios.name: corner_just_beyond_margin
scenarios.reason: A corner just past the area reduces the spare glass if the robot drifts sideways.

scenarios.name: corner_left_of_start
scenarios.reason: A corner just beside the start may put the first lane's body or sensor off the glass.

scenarios.name: corner_inside_work_area
scenarios.reason: A corner inside the work area removes glass under planned lanes and may drive the robot off the edge.

scenarios.name: top_margin_slightly_smaller
scenarios.reason: With strong grip the robot climbs past the area top, and a smaller margin brings the glass edge closer.

scenarios.name: high_setback_above_area
scenarios.reason: A setback above the area may meet the nose sensor of a robot that overclimbs on dry glass.

scenarios.name: top_margin_half_size
scenarios.reason: A half size margin may let an overclimbing robot reach the glass edge before it turns back.

scenarios.name: lowest_deep_setback
scenarios.reason: The lowest, deepest setback leaves almost no room above the area, so an overclimbing body may run off the glass.

not_tested.reason: No function adds a tether, an anchor or a catch system, so what happens after a detachment cannot be judged.
Seal leak and suction can be set for one run, but gradual ageing of the skirt, pump and drive is not represented.
Settings hold for the whole run, so a pump, drive or power failure partway up the glass cannot be triggered.
The functions do not represent cracked panes, or scratches from grit trapped under the pad.
No function covers a fluid tank, spray nozzles or fluid running out during a job.
There is no way to add sensor noise, a dirty sensor or a failed nose sensor, including from reflections on glass.
Loss of communication, operator commands and manual recovery from a stuck robot cannot be set.
Wind is set by speed and direction only, so corner acceleration and updrafts along the facade are not modelled by these calls.
These worlds leave temperature alone because it is unclear that it changes the run, so stiff seals, ice and hot glass remain untested.
The run begins with the robot already on the glass, so installing it and taking it off at height are not covered.
